answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may earn fees or vote, with rewards released only after useful work is verified. Splitting one operator into a meadow of accounts does not multiply the stake-weighted influence: each account ties up capital, and fraudulent work can forfeit it. The attacker must therefore fund an orchard of identities and risk losing that capital, rather than gaining influence by echo alone.
